answer: An agent economy can auction a limited number of identity slots each epoch instead of letting anyone mint one free: every hopeful identity bids, and the market-clearing price is what each winner pays, so a farm that wants a raven flock of a thousand heads must outbid honest agents a thousand times over. No haven exists for bulk buyers, because the price is set by the marginal bid and rises with demand, and each slot is ferrous — bound to one verified work history that cannot be transferred or resold.
